answer.rationale: Write-path p99 is 5x and isolated to the primary region during peak settlement, so the single intervention must restore write availability without dropping customer writes. Circuit breaking would shed writes and is rejected. Read-replica routing only helps if primary slowness is from read/report contention; it cannot move writes off a regionally degraded primary. Rollback is plausible given the 2h-old release but does not explain regional isolation and risks interrupting peak settlement writes. Pre-peak headroom is the wrong shape for a mid-incident write-path failure. Regional failover matches the blast radius and historically restored latency with a clean traffic shift. Cause is still uncertain (release vs regional vs load), and failing over at settlement peak can perturb downstream settlement, so keep this a standard-scale shift rather than a full untested cutover. Verifying b2 and b5 to check the failover and write-latency records before treating either as decisive.
